note: [M] sets up the Cauchy argument at a separated configuration on a common grid from the cutoff estimates of Definition D08. In [L] the point Cauchy property is a hypothesis `Purchased` of this part, supplied from the extraction (`Order.evaluated`), so the setup appears only as that hypothesis.

snippet.text: def Purchased (C:Family G)(e: Extraction.Sequence) : Prop:= ∀ (n p:ℕ) (v: Fin n→ C.book.Token) x, x∈Cyclic C.S p n → CauchySeq (fun i=> evaluate C e p v [] i x)

proof_context.conclusion: `Purchased` is the pointwise Cauchy property of the lattice values `evaluate C e p v [] i x` at every point of `Cyclic C.S p n`, the statement that [M]'s triangle-inequality argument proves.

snippet.text:
theorem positioned (M:FixedBounds C) (h:Purchased C e) : PositionsUV C e:=by
   intro p n v
   obtain ⟨f,hf,h⟩:= reachable M e h p v
   refine ⟨f,hf,fun t ht=>?_,fun l=>⟨h l,held (h l),fun t ht=>pudding e (h l) t ht⟩⟩
   have hk : Cluster C e p n (fun N => lifted C N p v) f:= h []
   exact ((pudding e hk t ht).2).congr' (Eventually.of_forall fun i=>at_probe p (e i) t v)

proof_context.conclusion: `positioned` takes `Purchased` and `FixedBounds` as hypotheses and concludes `PositionsUV`.
